# Penguin

> Penguin is a funny pedometer and step counter app for iPhone, published by Lightbulb Moment Labs, Inc. Your daily steps from Apple Health power a smug, overconfident cartoon penguin. It's "the pedometer for people who hate pedometers." Coming soon to the App Store.

Key facts:
- Platform: iPhone (iOS). Counts steps from Apple Health, so it works with just a phone or with an Apple Watch.
- Reads step count only. Step history stays on the device. No accounts, ads, analytics, or tracking.
- The penguin's form and attitude react to your steps. He stays round at every stage; progress shows up as swagger.
- Daily step goal with rest days that never cost progress ("Aura").
- The Locker: unlockable outfits. Optional Penguin Plus adds cosmetic outfits only, never extra progress.
- Expeditions: an endless map of landmarks unlocked by steps.
- Waddles: small friend groups that share goal progress through iCloud and can send pokes.
- Pricing has not been announced.
- Contact: hello@penguinathletics.com

## Learn: the health benefits of walking
Evidence-based, cited articles. Editorial policy: https://penguinathletics.com/learn/editorial-policy/

- [Walking and your heart](https://penguinathletics.com/learn/walking-heart-health/): Blood pressure, cholesterol, and the most underrated cardio on the planet.
- [Walking and longevity](https://penguinathletics.com/learn/walking-longevity/): How many steps buy you more years, and what the 10,000-step rule gets wrong.
- [Walking for weight loss](https://penguinathletics.com/learn/walking-weight-loss/): What walking really does for weight, blood sugar, and metabolism. No shame, just science.
- [Walking and your mind](https://penguinathletics.com/learn/walking-mental-health/): Stress, mood, sleep, and focus. A walk is the cheapest reset you own.
- [Walking basics](https://penguinathletics.com/learn/walking-basics/): How to start, stick with it, and maybe even like it. Built for people who hate exercise.

- [Does walking lower blood pressure?](https://penguinathletics.com/learn/does-walking-lower-blood-pressure/): Yes. A large Cochrane review of 73 trials found that regular walking lowered systolic blood pressure (the top number) by about 4 mmHg on average. Most of the walking programs in those trials averaged around 150 minutes of moderate walking a week for a few months.
